Dave's feelings are hurt when he overhears everyone talking about him behind his back.
As Matthew longs to become a gambler, Dave is tricked into introducing Bill at a big industry dinner.
Amidst some pre-April Fool's Day pranks, Bill tries to keep an important interview on track, while Lisa and Matthew vie for a key assignment and Beth learns she has a secret admirer.
As Beth seeks Jimmy's help negotiating a deal, Lisa goes after Dave for a raise.
When the kids won't do their chores, Adam and Andi decide to go on strike too.
When Adam thinks Kate's boyfriend, Tyler (Griffin Gluck), is a pothead, he decides to confront Tyler but doesn't get the support he expects from Andi.
When Adam needs to hire a new project manager, Andi accuses Adam of unconscious bias after he only interviews men for the job.
Adam and Andi try to get back in their neighbors' good graces after no one shows up to their potluck.
Carrie's boss, Pruzan, has his first big case as partner, and Carrie is overwhelmed with work.
Now that Arthur is back from the hospital, Carrie thinks that it is a good idea that she and Doug get life insurance.

This episode sets the time before Doug and Carrie's marriage. Carrie is very nervous to be married to Doug. She can not stop vomiting. When the two meet with the priest, he remembers Doug and Carrie met at camp as kids.
Deacon asks Doug to come along to Atlantic City for a weekend. Carrie wants to go salsa dancing with him, but grudgingly concurs with Doug's wishes and goes with them to Atlantic City.
Becker obsesses over whether or not younger women still find him attractive. Linda takes advantage of a hard-working temp.
Becker gets in hot water with parents when his nutrition lecture at an elementary school turns into a sex talk.
John gets a portable talking computer for his speech-impaired patient, with unintended consequences.
Becker bores a bartender with a story about his ex-wife's wedding.
Reggie decides to help Jake fulfill some of the dreams he had as a child, with disastrous consequences.
Dr. John Becker's laundry, apartment, and mail have all been tampered with and he is sure the culprit is one of his pesky neighbors.
Jack has second thoughts about hiring a rigorous personal trainer.
To impress an old high school classmate, Finch engineers a date with an emotionally vulnerable supermodel.
Finch struggles to get married before his fiancée's ex-boyfriend finds out.

Casey's husband, Stuart, returns after being gone for two years.
Joe and Helen find the house of their dreams.
When Adam's oldest daughter experiences a momentous occasion while Andi is unavailable, he tries to keep his cool and gingerly guide her through it.
Adam tries to pretend he isn't jealous when he discovers Andi has a close male friend at work.
When Andi and Marcy realize they were rivals in high school, Adam and Don are dragged into the feud and forced to take sides.
When Adam and Andi have the dreaded "talk" with Teddy and Kate, their awkward approach makes the kids horribly uncomfortable.
Doug (Kevin James) and Carrie (Leah Remini) are down on their luck; Carrie is still out of a job, money is tight and the refrigerator is broken.

Doug (Kevin James) and Carrie (Leah Remini) decide its only fair that Deacon (Victor Williams) and Kelly (Merrin Dungey) occasionally watch Arthur (Jerry Stiller) in exchange for babysitting their kids.

Carrie (Leah Remini) befriends Trish (Janeane Garofalo) an ex-girlfriend of Doug’s (Kevin James) in order to get a discount at Saks, but soon realizes why he dumped her-she is extremely needy and says the word 'literally' in every sentence.
While recovering in the hospital from an emergency appendectomy, Doug (Kevin James) is caught moaning the names of several women in his sleep.
Marcy regrets denting Steve's new car when he claims that she's made him impotent.

While secretly going through Steve and Marcy's mail, Al and Peggy fill out an application to a TV game show called "How Do I Love Thee" where the objective is a Bundy natural: surviving physical torture from one's spouse.
After going with Steve to the racetrack, Al is reluctant to reveal that he won $1,200 because he knows that Peggy and the kids will take the money for themselves.
Al's quiet three-day weekend plans to watch his favorite John Wayne movie "Hondo" are ruined when Peggy's eccentric relatives come to visit the Bundy household.
John has a dream that he and Chris kissed each other. At the office, Linda is late and tells Margaret it's because her cab got hit by a runaway hotdog cart.
Highlights from last season include Chris and John exchanging "I love yous" as Chris is wheeled into surgery for an appendectomy.
At the diner, Jake bemoans his poor financial status, and Hector proposes that he participates in a drug-testing program to earn money.
Chris and John have their first impromptu date, but Chris wants something more formal before taking the relationship any further, and tells John so.
